```text
  'nightly-container\tqueued\t\nnightly-binary\tqueued',
  '### What problem would this solve?\n' +
    '\n' +
    '**Summary**\n' +
    "The integration suite takes roughly 25–30 minutes for a full pass, so in practice almost nobody runs it before pushing; contributors push, wait on CI, and find out later. A run on 2026-09-14 consumed the default 10-minute `go test` timeout having completed about 252 of 700 top-level tests. Individual tests run far over the project's own target of sub-2s: thirteen exceeded 10 seconds, and two dominate — `TestActionsScopedWorkflows` at 1m17s and `TestActionsReusableWorkflow` at 50s, both single large blocks whose cost is fixture setup and git I/O rather than assertions. Nothing holds the line today: no budget, no ratchet, and no signal short of the whole CI job timing out.\n" +
    '\n' +
    '**User story**\n' +
    '"As a contributor, I want to run the integration tests relevant to my change and get an answer in under a minute so that I can iterate locally instead of using CI as my test runner."\n' +
    '\n' +
    '**Rough scope — Large**\n' +
    'Establishing which tests are parallel-safe is itself undocumented groundwork, and the work then spans the test harness, CI configuration, fixture design, and a new enforcement mechanism.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '**Source**\n' +
    'Analysis of a full `go test ./...` run of this fork on 2026-09-14, measured against the sub-2s target in `AGENTS.md`.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '### What do you propose?\n' +
    '\n' +
    '**Solution proposal**\n' +
    'Make the suite something developers actually run:\n' +
    '\n' +
    '- **Establish which tests are parallel-safe.** The rule separating tests that tolerate `t.Parallel()` from those needing serial DB state is currently written down nowhere. Document it, then enable parallelism where it is safe. This is groundwork for everything else here.\n' +
    '- **Sharding**, so CI can fan out across N workers and a developer can run a single shard locally.\n' +
    '- **Selective runs** targeting the area you changed, rather than all-or-nothing.\n' +
    '- **An enforced runtime budget.** The test logger already emits `+++ TestX is a slow test (run: …)` lines, so the data exists — turn it into a report, set a per-test ceiling, and fail CI on regressions past it.\n' +
    '- **Faster fixtures for the worst offenders.** Share repository fixtures across subtests in the two Actions tests instead of creating one per `t.Run`, and split them into independently runnable tests. Profile first to confirm setup is the cost rather than the `FlushAll(ctx, 5*time.Second)` calls.\n' +
    '- **Make standard tooling work.** A bare `go test ./...` currently dies at the 10-minute default with a goroutine dump and no failing assertion, because the 40-minute timeout lives only in `Makefile:82`. Either make it work or exit immediately pointing at `make test-integration`. A `testing.Short()` skip would give contributors a fast command that passes.',
  'CarsonRackley\n' +
    '## Problem\n' +
    '\n' +
    "`web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts` and `web_src/js/features/repo-issue-edit.test.ts` fail whenever vitest puts them in the same worker, and pass when it doesn't. Which files share a worker changes between runs, so the failure looks random.\n" +
    '\n' +
    '**Root cause.** `vitest.config.ts` sets `isolate: false`, so test files in one worker share modules and the same `document`. Both files call `initGlobalShortcut()` (`repo-issue-edit.test.ts` at module level, `shortcut.test.ts` in `beforeAll`). Each call adds two more `keydown` listeners to `document`, and they all dispatch into the same shared `globalRegistry`. After the second call, every key press runs its shortcut twice.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '**How I know:**\n' +
    '\n' +
    '- CI: the `sonarqube` job on #161 failed with `repo-issue-edit.test.ts &gt; r quotes the selection after the existing text, or only moves to the reply box`: `expected
... [3213 chars elided] ...
 it.\n' +
    "**Rationale:** A real page calls `initGlobalShortcut()` once, so the guard doesn't change production behaviour. It fixes both orders and protects future test files, and it's the smallest change.\n" +
    "**Consequences:** A second call silently does nothing, so a test can't re-initialize with fresh listeners. Other shared state in `globalRegistry` is unchanged; tests still need to unregister the shortcuts they add (both files already do).\n" +
    '\n' +
    '## Scope\n' +
    '\n' +
    'small, `scope: small`. One guard in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts`, one new unit test, and repeated runs for evidence. No production behaviour changes.\n' +
    '\n' +
    'Found while debugging CI on #161 (#118).\n' +
    '\n' +
    '---\n' +
```

```text
    'if [ -z "$SNAPCRAFT_PROJECT_NAME" ]; then\n' +
    '  echo "No snapcraft build env, continue with mocking ...."\n' +
    '  craftctl() { echo "* mocking craftctl: $*"; }\n' +
    '  snap() { echo "* mocking snap: $*"; }\n' +
    'else\n' +
    '  echo "Add working directory to git safe.directory ..."\n' +
    '  git config --global --add safe.directory "$PWD"\n' +
    'fi\n' +
    '\n' +
    '# How it works:\n' +
    '# * snapcraft.io checks out the default branch (e.g.: main during 1.27 dev period)\n' +
    '# * "override-pull" step gets the latest tag by date (e.g.: v1.26.1)\n' +
    '# * use "snap info gitea" to get the latest released tag\n' +
    '#   * if the latest tag is not released to stable, checkout that tag and build it for "stable"\n' +
    '#   * otherwise, build the main branch for "devel"\n' +
```

Here's a draft. In the course format it's a hardening task (not a bug report). I sized it medium, and the CI data I pulled backs that up.

**What I found on `main` (live, Nov 13):**
- `release-nightly-snapcraft` has failed or been cancelled on all 99 push runs, with no successes (78 failed, 21 cancelled). It fails with `fatal: empty string is not a valid pathspec` because `snap/part-gitea-pull.sh` assumes upstream's tags and Snap Store listing.
- `release-nightly` has run 99 times and never finished: 98 cancelled, 1 queued. Its jobs wait on upstream's private `namespace-profile-gitea-release-*` runners, which this repo doesn't have. Each new push cancels the one before.
- A push to `main` only runs `test-unit` and `sonarqube`. The sqlite, MySQL, Postgres and MSSQL integration jobs, the e2e tests and the frontend Vitest run all check for `pull_request`, so `main` never runs them.
- The `main` rulesets require one approval but no status checks, so a PR with red CI can still be merged.
- The `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` commit has no test runs at all, only skipped cron jobs. D8's Suite health asks for CI results at that tag, so right now the team has none to cite.

---

**Title:** Main's CI is red on every push and never runs the integration, e2e or frontend suites

```markdown
## Problem

Every push to `main` shows a red X, and the suites that would catch a broken merge never run there.

- **Upstream-only release workflows fail on every push.** `release-nightly-snapcraft` has failed or been cancelled on all 99 of its push runs to `main` (78 failed, 21 cancelled, 0 passed). The latest one, [run 43539275792](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43539275792), stops with `fatal: empty string is not a valid pathspec` in `snap/part-gitea-pull.sh`, which looks for upstream's release tags and its Snap Store listing. `release-nightly` has never finished: 98 runs were cancelled and 1 is queued ([example](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43537000589)). Its jobs wait for upstream's private `namespace-profile-gitea-release-*` runners, and the next push cancels them. `release-tag-rc` and `release-tag-version` use the same runners, so pushing our sprint tags queues them the same way. Because these fail on every push, people have stopped looking at `main`'s status, and a real failure would be lost among them.
- **Main never runs most of the test suites.** In `pull-db-tests.yml`, every integration job (`test-sqlite`, `test-mysql`, `test-pgsql`, `test-mssql`) has `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'`. `pull-e2e-tests.yml` and the frontend job in `pull-compliance.yml` run only on pull requests too. A push to `main` runs `test-unit` and `sonarqube` and nothing else ([run 43345969430](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43345969430): every integration job skipped). The PR rules don't require a branch to be up to date with `main`, so two PRs that pass on their own can break `main` once both are merged, and no run would show it.
- **No CI baseline for Suite health.** The Sprint 2 tag `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` (`40e0aa79`) has no test runs at all, only skipped cron jobs. D8 asks for each suite's summary line at that tag and at sprint end, "using CI results where available", and right now there are none.

## Goal

A push to `main` has a green status unless one of our own suites failed. `main` runs the sqlite integration, e2e and frontend unit suites after every merge, and anyone on the team can run those suites against any tag or branch to get a baseline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a push to `main`, when CI runs, then `release-nightly` and `release-nightly-snapcraft` show as skipped (not failed, cancelled or queued) because the repository is not `go-gitea/gitea`, and each skip condition has a same-line comment giving that reason.
- [ ] AC2: Given a pushed tag matching `release-tag-rc` / `release-tag-version`'s filters, when CI runs, then those workflows are skipped for the same reason and nothing sits queued waiting for a runner.
- [ ] AC3: Given a merge to `main`, when CI runs, then sqlite migration plus integration tests, the Playwright e2e suite and `make test-frontend` all run against the merged commit and report pass or fail.
- [ ] AC4: Given a team member opens Actions → "main suites" → Run workflow and enters a ref (e.g. `v1.27.3-csci435-s2`), when it finishes, then the same suites from AC3 have run against that ref.
- [ ] AC5: Given any run from AC3 or AC4, when it finishes, then each suite's job summary shows its runner's summary line (passed, failed and skipped counts), even if the suite failed, so D8 can quote it without digging through the logs.
- [ ] AC6: Given a pull request, when CI runs, then the set of jobs that run and whether each passes or fails are unchanged from before this issue (no new PR-time cost, no PR job removed).

## Out of Scope

- MySQL, Postgres and MSSQL integration runs on `main`. They stay PR-only to keep Actions minutes down.
- Making status checks required in the `main` ruleset. That needs repo-admin rights. I'll propose it to the team or the TA once AC3 is green on `main`.
- Making the integration suite faster (#37).
- Fixing any test that fails once it runs on `main`. Each failure group gets its own issue, as Suite health asks.

## Open Questions

- Should AC3 run on every merge, or on a nightly schedule to save minutes? The draft says every merge, because one run per merge points straight at the PR that broke `main`.

## Evidence of Fix

Broken or missing CI check: links to runs before and after.
- **Before:** the failed, cancelled and skipped runs linked under Problem.
- **After:** the first push to `main` after the merge, with the release workflows skipped and the three suites from AC3 run; a manual run (AC4) against `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` with its summary lines; and a pull request run showing the same jobs as before (AC6).

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: stopping the upstream release workflows

**Decision:** Add `if: github.repository == 'go-gitea/gitea'` to each job in the four release workflows, the same guard upstream already puts on `cron-renovate.yml` and the other cron jobs.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Delete the workflow files.* This is the smallest diff today, but it conflicts with any upstream sync that touches those files, and it removes the files from the repo for good.
- *Turn them off in the Actions settings (`gh workflow disable`).* No code changes, but nobody can review it, it only shows up in the settings page, any admin can switch it back on, and it's the kind of quiet silencing the course counts as small at most.
**Rationale:** These workflows publish upstream's binaries, Docker images and snap, so they can't run here and shouldn't. The guard is what upstream already does for fork-only cases, it goes through review in the diff, and a code comment records why it's there.
**Consequences:** If the team ever wants its own release builds, the guard has to come off and the workflows need new runners and secrets.

### Decision 2: running the suites on `main` and on demand

**Decision:** A new `main-suites.yml` workflow, triggered by `push` to `main` and by `workflow_dispatch` with a `ref` input, that runs the sqlite integration, e2e and frontend unit jobs.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Remove the `pull_request`-only conditions in `pull-db-tests.yml`, `pull-e2e-tests.yml` and `pull-compliance.yml`.* This reuses the existing jobs, but it changes three files that run on every PR, makes it harder to show AC6 holds, and still gives no way to test an old tag, because `files-changed` has nothing to compare against when the workflow is started by hand.
- *A nightly scheduled run.* It costs fewer minutes, but a failure could come from any of that day's merges, and it still can't be pointed at a tag.
**Rationale:** One new file covers AC3 and AC4 without touching the PR workflows, and the `ref` input is what makes a Suite health baseline possible.
**Consequences:** The job steps duplicate the ones in the PR workflows and can drift apart. A comment in each file points to the other.

## Scope

medium, `scope: medium`. Changes all four release workflows and adds one new workflow with three jobs and job summaries. No product code changes. Evidence comes from CI runs on `main`, a manual run against the Sprint 2 tag and a PR run, so it needs several pushes and a check of each run, not one quick edit.

---
_Drafted with Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) for @controlled-opposition._
```

**Check before posting:**
- **Scope:** Turning off the release workflows on its own would count as small at most. What makes this medium is AC3–AC5 (new coverage on `main` and the baseline you can run on any tag). Keep both parts together.
- **Overlap:** AC5 and the AC4 baseline run feed straight into the team's D8 Suite health section, which is a good reason to give for picking this issue.
- **Labels and milestone:** add `scope: medium`, the `Sprint 3` milestone and assign yourself. It also needs a teammate's spec review before you start coding.

Should I post it with `gh issue create` (exactly as written, or with your edits)? When this session is done, run `specstory sync` and file the log as the spec session for this issue.

```text
        ports:
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-14 01:49:13Z)**_

Yes, and the timings make a good case for it. On backend PRs the slowness comes from how the jobs are arranged, not from waiting for a runner. I timed the four recent pushes to #156's PR:

| Job | Run time | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `db-tests` (whole workflow) | **26–30 min** | Can't finish until `test-unit` and then `sonarqube` are done |
| `test-unit` | 23–27 min | Runs the race-detector unit tests twice in a row, once normally and once with `gogit` (about 12 min each) |
| `sonarqube` | waits 23–27 min, then 2–3 min | `needs: test-unit` |
| `test-mysql` / `test-mssql` / `test-pgsql` ×2 | 15–26 min each | All four run on every backend PR, even when it doesn't touch the database layer |
| `test-sqlite` | 15–21 min | One shard; Postgres is already split into two |
| `lint-backend` | 11–12 min | Runs alongside the tests, so it doesn't add to the total |
| `e2e-tests` | about 10 min | Not the bottleneck |

Waiting for a runner was about 20 seconds in every run except one compliance run that waited 113 min, which looks like a one-off. Frontend and docs PRs already finish in about 10 min.

**Plan:**
1. Split `test-unit` into two jobs that run at the same time. `sonarqube` waits only for the normal one.
2. Run MySQL, MSSQL and Postgres on a PR only when it touches the database layer. Every merge runs them on `main` instead, using the `main-suites.yml` workflow from the first draft, so no suite stops running anywhere.
3. Split sqlite into two shards, reusing the `TEST_SHARD` setup Postgres already has.

Together these should take a backend PR from about 28 min to about 15 min.

**About scope:** the course allows only one hardening issue per person, so I folded this into the same issue rather than splitting it into two. It's still `medium`, since the D1 sizes in COURSE-WORKFLOW.md are small or medium, and moving the database jobs ties it together naturally. To keep it doable by Nov 19, I moved the job-summary AC from the first draft to Out of Scope.

---

**Title:** Backend PRs wait about 28 minutes for CI, and main never runs the full test suites

```markdown
## Problem

CI is slow on pull requests, and `main` is both noisy and under-tested.

- **Backend PRs take 26–30 minutes.** On the last four pushes to #156's PR, `db-tests` took 29.6, 26.1, 28.4 and 29.8 minutes (e.g. [run 43524265133](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43524265133)). The slowest step is `test-unit` (22.8–26.6 min), which runs the race-detector unit tests twice in a row, once normally (12.1 min) and once with the `gogit` tag (11.5 min). `sonarqube` has `needs: test-unit`, so it waits 23–27 minutes before its 2–3 minute scan. MySQL, MSSQL and both Postgres shards (15–26 min each) run on every backend PR, including the ones that never touch `models/`. `test-sqlite` runs as one shard (15–21 min), while Postgres is already split in two. Waiting for a runner isn't the cause: in these runs, jobs started within about 20 seconds.
- **Upstream-only release workflows fail on every push to `main`.** `release-nightly-snapcraft` has failed or been cancelled on all 99 of its push runs (78 failed, 21 cancelled, 0 passed). The latest one, [run 43539275792](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43539275792), stops with `fatal: empty string is not a valid pathspec` in `snap/part-gitea-pull.sh`, which looks for upstream's release tags and its Snap Store listing. `release-nightly` has never finished: 98 runs were cancelled and 1 is queued ([example](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43537000589)). It waits for upstream's private `namespace-profile-gitea-release-*` runners, which `release-tag-rc` and `release-tag-version` also use. Because these fail on every push, people have stopped looking at `main`'s status, and a real failure would be lost among them.
- **Main never runs most of the test suites.** Every integration job in `pull-db-tests.yml` has `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'`, and `pull-e2e-tests.yml` and the frontend job in `pull-compliance.yml` run only on pull requests too. A push to `main` runs `test-unit` and `sonarqube` and nothing else ([run 43345969430](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43345969430)). The Sprint 2 tag `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` (`40e0aa79`) has no test runs at all, so D8's Suite health section has no CI baseline to quote.

## Goal

A backend PR's checks finish in about half the time they take now, and no test suite stops running anywhere: anything taken off PRs runs on every merge to `main`. `main` is green unless one of our own suites failed, and anyone on the team can run the full suite against any tag.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a push to `main` or a pushed tag, when CI runs, then `release-nightly`, `release-nightly-snapcraft`, `release-tag-rc` and `release-tag-version` show as skipped (not failed, cancelled or queued), and each skip condition has a same-line comment saying the workflow only runs upstream.
- [ ] AC2: Given a backend PR, when `db-tests` runs, then the normal and `gogit` unit test passes run as two separate jobs at the same time, and `sonarqube` starts as soon as the normal one finishes.
- [ ] AC3: Given a backend PR that changes nothing under `models/`, `modules/setting/` or `services/migrations/`, when `db-tests` runs, then it runs the sqlite migration and integration tests in two shards, and the MySQL, MSSQL and Postgres jobs are skipped with a same-line comment pointing to this issue.
- [ ] AC4: Given a backend PR that does change a file under those paths, when `db-tests` runs, then the MySQL, MSSQL and both Postgres jobs still run, the same as before this issue.
- [ ] AC5: Given four backend PR runs that fall under AC3, when they finish, then the median wall-clock time of `db-tests` is at most 15 minutes (it is 26–30 minutes now), and all four runs finish with the same pass/fail result they would have had before.
- [ ] AC6: Given a merge to `main`, when CI runs, then sqlite, MySQL, MSSQL and Postgres migration plus integration tests, the Playwright e2e suite and `make test-frontend` all run against the merged commit, so every suite taken off PRs still runs after every merge.
- [ ] AC7: Given a team member opens Actions → "main suites" → Run workflow and enters a ref (e.g. `v1.27.3-csci435-s2`), when it finishes, then the same suites from AC6 have run against that ref.

## Out of Scope

- Writing each suite's pass/fail/skip counts to the job summary. Useful for D8, but a follow-up.
- Making status checks required in the `main` ruleset. That needs repo-admin rights. I'll propose it to the team or the TA once AC6 is green.
- Making individual integration tests faster, e.g. the two slow Actions tests (#37).
- Speeding up `lint-backend` (11–12 min). It runs alongside the tests, so it doesn't make the total longer.
- Fixing any test that fails once it runs on `main`. Each failure group gets its own issue, as Suite health asks.

## Open Questions

- Are `models/`, `modules/setting/` and `services/migrations/` the right paths to trigger the full database set in AC3/AC4? Any SQL written by hand elsewhere would be missed until it reaches `main`.
- Should AC6 run on every merge or nightly? The draft says every merge, so a failure points straight at the PR that caused it.

## Evidence of Fix

Broken or missing CI check: links to runs before and after.
- **Before:** the runs linked under Problem, and the four `db-tests` times from #156 (26.1–29.8 min).
- **After:** four backend PR runs under AC3 with their times and median (AC5); one PR run that changes `models/` and still runs all databases (AC4); the first push to `main` after the merge, with the release workflows skipped and every suite from AC6 run; and a manual run against `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` (AC7).

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: stopping the upstream release workflows

**Decision:** Add `if: github.repository == 'go-gitea/gitea'` to each job in the four release workflows, the same guard upstream already puts on `cron-renovate.yml`.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Delete the workflow files.* This is the smallest diff today, but it conflicts with any upstream sync that touches those files, and it removes them from the repo for good.
- *Turn them off in the Actions settings (`gh workflow disable`).* Nobody can review it, it only shows up in the settings page, any admin can switch it back on, and it's the kind of quiet silencing the course counts as small at most.
**Rationale:** These workflows publish upstream's binaries, Docker images and snap, so they can't run here and shouldn't. The guard is what upstream already does for forks, and the reason goes in a code comment.
**Consequences:** If the team ever wants its own release builds, the guard has to come off and the workflows need new runners and secrets.

### Decision 2: cutting backend PR time

**Decision:** Split `test-unit` into two jobs that run at the same time, run the extra databases on a PR only when it changes the database layer, and split sqlite into two shards using the `TEST_SHARD` setup Postgres already has.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Split everything into more shards and change nothing else.* Each PR would finish sooner but use more runners for the same work, and the org's limit on jobs running at once would start making PRs wait for each other.
- *Drop the `-race` flag or the `gogit` pass on PRs.* That would save the most time, but it removes checks without fixing anything, and the course counts that as silencing.
**Rationale:** The total time is the longest chain of jobs that wait on each other, and right now that's the two unit-test passes in a row plus Sonar waiting for both. Running them side by side shortens that chain without dropping any check. Most of our PRs change templates, routers or services, where the four databases behave the same, so sqlite covers them; database-specific bugs come from `models/`, and those PRs still get every database.
**Consequences:** A database-specific bug outside those paths now shows up on `main` right after the merge, not on the PR. AC6 makes sure it's caught on the next merge and points at the PR that caused it.

### Decision 3: running the suites on `main` and on demand

**Decision:** A new `main-suites.yml` workflow, triggered by `push` to `main` and by `workflow_dispatch` with a `ref` input.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Remove the `pull_request`-only conditions in the existing PR workflows.* This reuses those jobs, but it mixes push and PR logic in files Decision 2 is already changing, and it can't test an old tag, because `files-changed` has nothing to compare against when started by hand.
- *A nightly scheduled run.* It costs fewer minutes, but a failure could come from any of that day's merges, and it still can't be pointed at a tag.
**Rationale:** One new file covers AC6 and AC7, and the `ref` input is what makes a Suite health baseline possible.
**Consequences:** The job steps duplicate the ones in the PR workflows and can drift apart. A comment in each file points to the other.

## Scope

medium, `scope: medium`. Changes `pull-db-tests.yml`, `files-changed.yml` and the four release workflows, and adds `main-suites.yml`. No product code changes. Evidence comes from timed PR runs, a run on `main` and a manual run against a tag, so it needs several pushes and a check of each run, not one edit.
```

```text
     1	name: release-nightly-snapcraft

#### release-nightly.yml
     1	name: release-nightly
     2	
     3	on:
     4	  push:
     5	    branches: [main, release/v*]
     6	
     7	concurrency:
     8	  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
     9	  cancel-in-progress: true
    10	
    11	jobs:
    12	  nightly-binary:
    13	    runs-on: namespace-profile-gitea-release-binary
    14	    permissions:
    15	      contents: read
    16	      id-token: write
    17	    steps:
    18	      - uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
    19	      # fetch all commits instead of only the last as some branches are long lived and could have many between versions
    20	      # fetch all tags to ensure that "git describe" reports expected Gitea version, eg. v1.21.0-dev-1-g1234567
    21	      - run: git fetch --unshallow --quiet --tags --force
    22	      - uses: actions/setup-go@924ae3a1cded613372ab5595356fb5720e22ba16 # v6.5.0
    23	        with:
    24	          go-version-file: go.mod
    25	          check-latest: true
    26	      - uses: ./.github/actions/node-setup
    27	      - run: make deps-frontend deps-backend
    28	      # xgo build
    29	      - run: make release
    30	        env:
    31	          TAGS: bindata
    32	      - name: Install Cosign
    33	        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@6f9f17788090df1f26f669e9d70d6ae9567deba6 # v4.1.2
    34	      - name: import gpg key
    35	        id: import_gpg
    36	        uses: crazy-max/ghaction-import-gpg@2dc316deee8e90f13e1a351ab510b4d5bc0c82cd # v7.0.0
    37	        with:
    38	          gpg_private_key: ${{ secrets.GPGSIGN_KEY }}
    39	          passphrase: ${{ secrets.GPGSIGN_PASSPHRASE }}
    40	      - name: sign binaries
    41	        env:
    42	          GPG_FINGERPRINT: ${{ steps.import_gpg.outputs.fingerprint }}
    43	          GPG_PASSPHRASE: ${{ secrets.GPGSIGN_PASSPHRASE }}
    44	        run: |
    45	          for f in dist/release/*; do
    46	            cosign sign-blob "$f" --bundle "$f.sigstore.json" --yes
    47	            echo "$GPG_PASSPHRASE" | gpg --pinentry-mode loopback --passphrase-fd 0 --batch --yes --detach-sign -u "$GPG_FINGERPRINT" --output "$f.asc" "$f"
    48	          done
    49	      # clean branch name to get the folder name in S3
    50	      - name: Get cleaned branch name
    51	        id: clean_name
    52	        env:
    53	          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
    54	        run: |
    55	          REF_NAME=$(echo "$REF" | sed -e 's/refs\/heads\///' -e 's/refs\/tags\///' -e 's/release\/v//')
    56	          echo "Cleaned name is ${REF_NAME}"
    57	          echo "branch=${REF_NAME}-nightly" &gt;&gt; "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    58	      - name: configure aws
    59	        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@254c19bd240aabef8777f48595e9d2d7b972184b # v6.2.1
    60	        with:
    61	          aws-region: ${{ secrets.AWS_REGION }}
    62	          aws-access-key-id: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
    63	          aws-secret-access-key: ${{ secrets.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
    64	      - name: upload binaries to s3
    65	        env:
    66	          AWS_S3_BUCKET: ${{ secrets.AWS_S3_BUCKET }}
    67	          BRANCH: ${{ steps.clean_name.outputs.branch }}
    68	        run: |
    69	          aws s3 sync dist/release "s3://$AWS_S3_BUCKET/gitea/$BRANCH" --no-progress
    70	
    71	  nightly-container:
    72	    runs-on: namespace-profile-gitea-release-docker
    73	    permissions:
    74	      contents: read
    75	      packages: write # to publish to ghcr.io
    76	    steps:
    77	      - uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
    78	      # fetch all commits instead of only the last as some branches are long lived and could have many between versions
    79	      # fetch all tags to ensure that "git describe" reports expected Gitea version, eg. v1.21.0-dev-1-g1234567
    80	      - run: git fetch --unshallow --quiet --tags --force
    81	      - uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@96fe6ef7f33517b61c61be40b68a1882f3264fb8 # v4.2.0
    82	      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@bb05f3f5519dd87d3ba754cc423b652a5edd6d2c # v4.2.0
    83	      - name: Get cleaned branch name
    84	        id: clean_name
    85	        env:
    86	          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
    87	        run: |
    88	          REF_NAME=$(echo "$REF" | sed -e 's/refs\/heads\///' -e 's/refs\/tags\///' -e 's/release\/v//')
    89	          echo "branch=${REF_NAME}-nightly" &gt;&gt; "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    90	      - uses: docker/metadata-action@dc802804100637a589fabce1cb79ff13a1411302 # v6.2.0
    91	        id: meta
    92	        with:
    93	          images: |-
    94	            gitea/gitea
    95	            ghcr.io/go-gitea/gitea
    96	          tags: |
    97	            type=raw,value=${{ steps.clean_name.outputs.branch }}
    98	          annotations: |
    99	            org.opencontainers.image.authors="maintainers@gitea.io"
   100	      - uses: docker/metadata-action@dc802804100637a589fabce1cb79ff13a1411302 # v6.2.0
   101	        id: meta_rootless
   102	        with:
   103	          images: |-
   104	            gitea/gitea
   105	            ghcr.io/go-gitea/gitea
   106	          # each tag below will have the suffix of -rootless
   107	          flavor: |
   108	            suffix=-rootless
   109	          tags: |
   110	            type=raw,value=${{ steps.clean_name.outputs.branch }}
   111	          annotations: |
   112	            org.opencontainers.image.authors="maintainers@gitea.io"
   113	      - name: Login to Docker Hub
   114	        uses: docker/login-action@c99871dec2022cc055c062a10cc1a1310835ceb4 # v4.3.0
   115	        with:
   116	          username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
   117	          password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}
   118	      - name: Login to GHCR using PAT
   119	        uses: docker/login-action@c99871dec2022cc055c062a10cc1a1310835ceb4 # v4.3.0
   120	        with:
   121	          registry: ghcr.io
   122	          username: ${{ github.repository_owner }}
   123	          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
   124	      - name: build regular docker image
   125	        uses: docker/build-push-action@53b7df96c91f9c12dcc8a07bcb9ccacbed38856a # v7.3.0
   126	        with:
   127	          context: .
   128	          platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64,linux/riscv64
   129	          push: true
   130	          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
   131	          annotations: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.annotations }}
   132	          cache-from: type=registry,ref=ghcr.io/go-gitea/gitea:buildcache-rootful
   133	          cache-to: type=registry,ref=ghcr.io/go-gitea/gitea:buildcache-rootful,mode=max
   134	      - name: build rootless docker image
   135	        uses: docker/build-push-action@53b7df96c91f9c12dcc8a07bcb9ccacbed38856a # v7.3.0
   136	        with:
   137	          context: .
   138	          platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64,linux/riscv64
   139	          push: true
   140	          file: Dockerfile.rootless
   141	          tags: ${{ steps.meta_rootless.outputs.tags }}
   142	          annotations: ${{ steps.meta_rootless.outputs.annotations }}
   143	          cache-from: type=registry,ref=ghcr.io/go-gitea/gitea:buildcache-rootless
   144	          cache-to: type=registry,ref=ghcr.io/go-gitea/gitea:buildcache-rootless,mode=max
```

```text
     4	# Caches are ref-scoped: PR runs read their own scope then fall back to the
     5	# base branch. Per .github/actions/go-cache/action.yml, PRs are restore-only,
     6	# so push-to-main is the only opportunity to populate the fallback scope.

#### actions/go-cache/action.yml
     1	name: go-caches
     2	description: Restore the go module, build, and golangci-lint caches. Save only on the cache-seeder workflow.
     3	
     4	# Only the cache-seeder workflow saves; rename requires updating cache-seeder.yml.
     5	# The lint job restores but does not save the gobuild cache, so only one writer
     6	# (the gobuild job) populates it and there is no contention on the cache key.
     7	# Seeder restores by exact key only (no restore-keys) so each go.sum seeds a clean
     8	# cache and size stays bounded; do not add restore-keys here. PR runs keep them.
     9	
    10	inputs:
    11	  lint-cache:
    12	    description: Restore (and save in cache-seeder) ~/.cache/golangci-lint
    13	    default: "false"
    14	
    15	runs:
    16	  using: composite
    17	  steps:
    18	    - if: ${{ github.workflow == 'cache-seeder' }}
    19	      uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
    20	      with:
    21	        path: ~/go/pkg/mod
    22	        key: gomod-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('go.sum') }}
    23	    - if: ${{ github.workflow != 'cache-seeder' }}
    24	      uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
    25	      with:
    26	        path: ~/go/pkg/mod
    27	        key: gomod-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('go.sum') }}
    28	        restore-keys: gomod-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}
    29	    - if: ${{ github.workflow == 'cache-seeder' &amp;&amp; inputs.lint-cache != 'true' }}
    30	      uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
    31	      with:
    32	        path: ~/.cache/go-build
    33	        key: gobuild-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('go.sum') }}
    34	    - if: ${{ github.workflow != 'cache-seeder' || inputs.lint-cache == 'true' }}
    35	      uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
    36	      with:
    37	        path: ~/.cache/go-build
    38	        key: gobuild-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('go.sum') }}
    39	        restore-keys: gobuild-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}
    40	    - if: ${{ inputs.lint-cache == 'true' &amp;&amp; github.workflow == 'cache-seeder' }}
    41	      uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
    42	      with:
    43	        path: ~/.cache/golangci-lint
    44	        key: golint-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('go.sum', '.golangci.yml') }}
    45	    - if: ${{ inputs.lint-cache == 'true' &amp;&amp; github.workflow != 'cache-seeder' }}
    46	      uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
    47	      with:
    48	        path: ~/.cache/golangci-lint
    49	        key: golint-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('go.sum', '.golangci.yml') }}
    50	        restore-keys: golint-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}
```

```text
     1	#!/bin/bash
     2	set -euo pipefail
     3	
     4	# Run a compiled *.test binary. When TEST_SHARD is set, enumerate top-level
     5	# tests via -test.list and run only the shard's slice; TestMain skips
     6	# environment setup in -test.list mode. Without TEST_SHARD, runs the binary
     7	# directly.
     8	
     9	BINARY=${1:?usage: $0 BINARY}
    10	
    11	if [ -z "${TEST_SHARD:-}" ]; then
    12	  exec "$BINARY"
    13	fi
    14	
    15	if ! [[ "${TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS:-}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
    16	  echo "TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS must be a positive integer, got: ${TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS:-}" &gt;&amp;2
    17	  exit 2
    18	fi
    19	if ! [[ "$TEST_SHARD" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || [ "$TEST_SHARD" -gt "$TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS" ]; then
    20	  echo "TEST_SHARD must be in [1, $TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS], got: $TEST_SHARD" &gt;&amp;2
    21	  exit 2
    22	fi
    23	
    24	NAMES=$("$BINARY" -test.list='^Test' | LC_ALL=C sort -u | awk -v r=$((TEST_SHARD - 1)) -v t="$TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS" '(NR - 1) % t == r')
    25	if [ -z "$NAMES" ]; then
    26	  echo "shard $TEST_SHARD/$TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS has no tests assigned" &gt;&amp;2
    27	  exit 1
    28	fi
    29	PATTERN=$(echo "$NAMES" | paste -sd '|' -)
    30	echo "Running shard $TEST_SHARD/$TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS ($(echo "$NAMES" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') tests)"
    31	exec "$BINARY" -test.run "^($PATTERN)\$"
```

```text
.PHONY: go-licenses
go-licenses: $(GO_LICENSE_FILE) ## regenerate go licenses

$(GO_LICENSE_FILE): go.mod go.sum
	GO=$(GO) $(GO) run build/generate-go-licenses.go $(GO_LICENSE_FILE)

.PHONY: test-integration
test-integration:
	@# Use a compiled binary: testlogger forwards gitea logs to t.Log, so `go test -v`
	@# would flood output per passing test. testcache can't help these tests anyway —
	@# they mutate the work directory, so cache inputs change between runs.
	$(GO) test $(GOTEST_FLAGS) -tags '$(TAGS)' -c gitea.dev/tests/integration -o ./test-integration-$(GITEA_TEST_DATABASE).test
	./tools/test-integration.sh ./test-integration-$(GITEA_TEST_DATABASE).test

.PHONY: test-integration-compile
test-integration-compile:
	$(GO) test $(GOTEST_FLAGS) -tags '$(TAGS)' -c -o /dev/null gitea.dev/tests/integration

.PHONY: test-integration\#%
test-integration\#%:
	$(GO) test $(GOTEST_FLAGS) -tags '$(TAGS)' -run $(subst .,/,$*) gitea.dev/tests/integration

.PHONY: test-migration
test-migration: migrations.integration.test migrations.individual.test

.PHONY: migrations.integration.test
migrations.integration.test:
	$(GO) test $(GOTEST_FLAGS) -tags '$(TAGS)' gitea.dev/tests/integration/migration-test

.PHONY: migrations.individual.test
migrations.individual.test:
	@# tests of multiple packages use the same database, don't run in parallel
	$(GO) test $(GOTEST_FLAGS) -tags '$(TAGS)' -p 1 $(MIGRATE_TEST_PACKAGES)

.PHONY: migrations.individual.test\#%
migrations.individual.test\#%:
	$(GO) test $(GOTEST_FLAGS) -tags '$(TAGS)' gitea.dev/models/migrations/$*

.PHONY: playwright
playwright: deps-frontend
	@CONTAINER_RUNTIME=$(CONTAINER_RUNTIME) ./tools/test-e2e.sh install

.PHONY: test-e2e
test-e2e: playwright frontend backend
	@CONTAINER_RUNTIME=$(CONTAINER_RUNTIME) EXECUTABLE=$(EXECUTABLE) ./tools/test-e2e.sh run $(GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS)

.PHONY: build
watch-backend: ## watch backend files and continuously rebuild
	GITEA_RUN_MODE=dev $(GO) run $(AIR_PACKAGE) -c .air.toml

.PHONY: test-backend
test-backend: ## test backend files
	@echo "Running go test with $(GOTEST_FLAGS) -tags '$(TAGS)'..."
	@$(GO) test $(GOTEST_FLAGS) -tags='$(TAGS)' $(GO_TEST_PACKAGES)

.PHONY: test-frontend
test-frontend: node_modules ## test frontend files
	pnpm exec vitest

.PHONY: test-check
test-check:
	@echo "Running test-check...";
	@diff=$$(git status -s); \
	if [ -n "$$diff" ]; then \
		echo "make test-backend has changed files in the source tree:"; \
		printf "%s" "$${diff}"; \
		echo "You should change the tests to create these files in a temporary directory."; \
		echo "Do not simply add these files to .gitignore"; \
		exit 1; \
	fi

.PHONY: test-backend\#%
test-backend\#%:
	@echo "Running go test with -tags '$(TAGS)'..."
	@$(GO) test $(GOTEST_FLAGS) -tags='$(TAGS)' -run $(subst .,/,$*) $(GO_TEST_PACKAGES)

.PHONY: coverage
coverage:
	grep '^\(mode: .*\)\|\(.*:[0-9]\+\.[0-9]\+,[0-9]\+\.[0-9]\+ [0-9]\+ [0-9]\+\)$$' coverage.out &gt; coverage-bodged.out
	grep '^\(mode: .*\)\|\(.*:[0-9]\+\.[0-9]\+,[0-9]\+\.[0-9]\+ [0-9]\+ [0-9]\+\)$$' integration.coverage.out &gt; integration.coverage-bodged.out
	$(GO) run tools/gocovmerge.go integration.coverage-bodged.out coverage-bodged.out &gt; coverage.all

.PHONY: unit-test-coverage
unit-test-coverage:
	@echo "Running unit-test-coverage $(GOTEST_FLAGS) -tags '$(TAGS)'..."
	@$(GO) test $(GOTEST_FLAGS) -tags='$(TAGS)' -cover -coverprofile coverage.out $(GO_TEST_PACKAGES) &amp;&amp; echo "\n==&gt;\033[32m Ok\033[m\n" || exit 1

.PHONY: tidy

shard:
tests/integration/integration_test.go:79:	// -test.list must skip InitIntegrationTest, which requires a database.
tests/integration/integration_test.go:81:	if flag.Lookup("test.list").Value.String() != "" {</result>
```

```text
func TestRepoCalendar(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()
	defer timeutil.MockSet(time.Date(2026, 10, 7, 12, 0, 0, 0, setting.DefaultUILocation))()

	session := loginUser(t, "user2")
	setDeadline := func(index int64, date string) {
		req := NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", fmt.Sprintf("/user2/repo1/issues/%d/deadline", index), map[string]string{"deadline": date})
		session.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK)
	}
	// user2/repo1 holds issue #1 and pull #2, neither with a deadline in the fixtures
	deadlines := map[int64]string{1: "2026-10-06", 2: "2026-10-30"}
	for index, date := range deadlines {
		setDeadline(index, date)
	}
	defer func() { // the issue indexer outlives the test database, so leave it as the fixtures had it
		for index := range deadlines {
			setDeadline(index, "")
		}
	}()

	t.Run("shows issues and pulls on their days", func(t *testing.T) {
		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/calendar"), http.StatusOK)
		doc := NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body)
		var links []string
		doc.Find(".repo-calendar-day:not(.is-other-month) .repo-calendar-entry").Each(func(_ int, a *goquery.Selection) {
			links = append(links, a.AttrOr("href", ""))
		})
		assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{"/user2/repo1/issues/1", "/user2/repo1/pulls/2"}, links)
		// a timezone bug would shift an entry into the neighbouring day cell
		assert.Equal(t, 1, doc.Find(`.repo-calendar-day:has(time[datetime="2026-10-06"]) a.repo-calendar-entry[href="/user2/repo1/issues/1"]`).Length())
		assert.Equal(t, 1, doc.Find(`.repo-calendar-day:has(time[datetime="2026-10-30"]) a.repo-calendar-entry[href="/user2/repo1/pulls/2"]`).Length())
		assert.Equal(t, 1, doc.Find(".repo-calendar-entry.is-pull").Length())
		assert.Equal(t, 1, doc.Find(".repo-calendar-day.is-today").Length())
	})

	t.Run("a crowded day folds extra entries into +N more", func(t *testing.T) {
		crowded := []int64{1, 2, 4, 5} // issue 1, pull 2, closed issue 4, pull 5
		for _, index := range crowded {
			setDeadline(index, "2026-10-14")
		}
		defer func() {
			for _, index := range crowded {
				setDeadline(index, "")
			}
			setDeadline(1, deadlines[1]) // back to the shared setup
			setDeadline(2, deadlines[2])
		}()
		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/calendar?state=all"), http.StatusOK)
		doc := NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body)
		cell := doc.Find(`.repo-calendar-day:has(time[datetime="2026-10-14"])`)
		assert.Equal(t, 3, cell.ChildrenFiltered("a.repo-calendar-entry").Length())
		more := cell.ChildrenFiltered("details.repo-calendar-more")
		assert.Equal(t, 1, more.Length())
		assert.Equal(t, 1, more.Find(".repo-calendar-more-list a.repo-calendar-entry").Length())
	})

	t.Run("month navigation keeps the filters", func(t *testing.T) {
		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/calendar?month=2026-09&amp;state=all"), http.StatusOK)
		doc := NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body)
		assert.Zero(t, doc.Find(".repo-calendar-day:not(.is-other-month) .repo-calendar-entry").Length())
		next, _ := doc.Find(`.list-header a[href*="month=2026-10"]`).First().Attr("href") // the next-month arrow</result>
```

I found two outright errors in the draft (claim 2's rc workflow, and claim 3's "vitest is PR-only"). Proposal C would have missed a real, repeated pgsql-only failure. B plus C on the current setup won't reach the ≤15 min target in E. Everything below was checked against the workflow files and the full run list (3,400 runs, Jul 27 to Nov 14), using only read-only calls.

## 1. Claims

**Claim 1: PARTLY (the numbers are right, the cause needs tightening).**
- 99 runs is the workflow's whole history (total_count 99, first run Jul 27): 78 failures, 21 cancellations, 0 successes.
- The 21 cancellations come from `cancel-in-progress: true` on a per-ref group (`release-nightly-snapcraft.yml:9-11`) during bursts of merges.
- Exact cause, from run 43539275792, step `snapcore/action-build`: `snap/part-gitea-pull.sh:33` reads `git for-each-ref --format '%(tag)'`. `%(tag)` is empty for lightweight tags, and all three fork tags (s0, s1, s2) are lightweight (`git cat-file -t` returns `commit`). So `last_committed_tag=""`.
  - `last_released_tag` comes from upstream's snap store entry (line 34) and is not empty. The two differ, so line 40 runs `git checkout ""`, which gives "fatal: empty string is not a valid pathspec".
- So the cause is lightweight or missing tags, not missing upstream tags as such. Even with annotated tags it would build our tag and then fail at publish: `SNAPCRAFT_STORE_CREDENTIALS` is unset (the only repo secret is `SONAR_TOKEN`), and the `gitea` snap name belongs to upstream.

**Claim 2: PARTLY WRONG.**
- release-nightly: 98 cancelled and 1 queued is correct. 77 of the cancellations came from the concurrency group when the next push landed. 21 hit GitHub's 24-hour queue limit.
- **release-tag-rc does not match our tags.** Its pattern `v1*-rc*` (`release-tag-rc.yml:6`) needs `-rc` in the name, and the workflow has 0 runs ever.
- Only release-tag-version matches: `v1.*`, minus `!v1*-rc*` and `!v1*-dev` (`release-tag-version.yml:5-8`). It has already fired for every course tag:
  - 35251424595 (s0), cancelled after 4 minutes
  - 37872246874 (s1), cancelled after 24 hours
  - 40956082407 (s2), cancelled after 24 hours
- So this is something that already happened three times, not a future risk.

**Claim 3: PARTLY WRONG.**
- Integration gating is correct: lines 20, 56, 91, 188 and 236 all require `github.event_name == 'pull_request'`. e2e and compliance are PR-only.
- But **vitest does run on main.** The sonarqube job runs `frontend-coverage` (`pull-db-tests.yml:279-280`) on every push, and it has failed main twice (see finding 1).
- No test runs exist for SHA 40e0aa79: correct. That commit is the merge of PR #133 (docs), made before the push trigger existed; the first push-triggered db-tests run was Nov 7.

**Claim 4: CONFIRMED, and worse than stated.**
- Ruleset `main-2` requires 1 approval, dismisses stale reviews and requires thread resolution. There are no status-check rules (`gh api repos/.../rules/branches/main`).
- Both rulesets have `bypass_actors: null`. There is no tag ruleset, so anyone with write access can push `v1.*` tags.

**Claim 5: PARTLY.**
- Wall time for full backend runs is 23.3 to 30.1 min (one outlier at 43.3), median about 27.6, so "26-30" is a little narrow.
- Queue time is confirmed negligible: median 2 s, maximum 1.8 min.
- Across 8 runs the two passes are 9.6-12.1 min (default) and 9.4-11.5 min (gogit). The quoted 12.1 / 11.5 is the slowest run.
- "Critical path is test-unit → sonarqube" is only mostly true. The integration jobs run 16-27 min:
  - In 43273685850, test-mysql (24.4) beat test-unit plus sonar (18.8 + 2.1).
  - In 43104714694, mysql (27.2) tied with test-unit plus sonar (24.8 + 3).
  - pgsql-shard-1 is consistently 20-22.
- In the 43524265133 log, **each pass spends about 3.6 min compiling** before the first package result (23:07:27 → 23:11:05, and 23:19:30 → 23:23:06). Real test execution is about 8 min per pass. See finding 2 for why.

## 2. Proposals

**A (repository guard): works, low risk.** It is upstream's own idiom (`cron-*.yml:11`, `giteabot.yml:55`). The repo is not a GitHub fork (`fork:false`), so the guard is fine. release-tag-rc needs no change for our tags; guard it anyway for consistency. Runs will still be created and skipped, which is only noise.

**B (split test-unit into two parallel jobs): works, but saves only 1-5 min on its own.**
- Each new job pays about 2.5 min of setup, about 3.6 min of compile and the 5 service containers.
- Expected result: the default job about 15-16 min, plus sonar 2-3 → **about 18 min**, while mssql, mysql and pgsql-shard-1 still take 20-27.
- Things to handle in the change:
  - sonarqube's condition `needs.test-unit.result != 'skipped'` (line 281) needs the new job name.
  - `make test-check` must run in both jobs.
  - Upload coverage only from the default job.
- Cheaper alternative: run the gogit pass only on push to main or only when `modules/git/**` changes.

**C (run mysql/mssql/pgsql only for DB paths): the path filter is unsafe, as the run history shows.**
- TestMilestoneBurndown/RealLifecycle failed **only on pgsql** three times, on three different branches (runs 37861291323 [both attempts], 38276920412, 40424442743). TestRepoCalendar failed only on pgsql in 42658314475.
- The code under test lives in `services/issue/milestone_burndown.go`, `routers/web/repo/milestone.go` and the routers calendar code. None of that matches `models/`, `modules/setting/` or `services/migrations/`, so C would have shipped these failures to main without a signal.
- Sharding sqlite does work. `make test-integration` always goes through `tools/test-integration.sh` (Makefile:451-456), which shards on `TEST_SHARD`, and `tests/integration/integration_test.go:79-81` skips DB setup in `-test.list` mode.
- Sharding caveats:
  - Each shard repeats go-setup (about 2 min), `make backend` (1.5-2.6 min) and the integration binary compile.
  - Shards are round-robin by test name, not by duration: pgsql shard 1 takes 17-20 min against 12-17 for shard 2 (shard 1 also runs the migration tests).
  - Run migration tests in only one shard.
- Safer alternative: keep all databases on PRs but shard mysql and mssql too. Or run the other databases on every PR that touches `**/*.go` outside `routers/web` templates. Or run them only on main (via D) and accept detection after merge.

**D (main-suites.yml on push and dispatch): workable, but don't copy the jobs.**
- A dispatch with a `ref` input plus `actions/checkout` with that ref works for s2: `.github/actions/*` and `tools/test-integration.sh` exist at the tag, and local composite actions resolve from the checked-out tree.
- `gh workflow run --ref <tag>` would not work, because the workflow file doesn't exist at old tags.
- Better: turn the job bodies of `pull-db-tests.yml` into a `workflow_call` workflow, or relax the `github.event_name == 'pull_request'` gates to `!= 'push' || <main-suite flag>` and add a `workflow_dispatch` input. Duplicated jobs will drift.
- Load risk: the repo is a public org repo, so the free-plan limit is 20 concurrent jobs. On Nov 13, five merges landed between 01:25 and 01:40. Five runs of about 8 jobs each would push PR jobs into a queue. Use `concurrency: {group: main-suites, cancel-in-progress: false}`, which collapses pending runs to the newest one; later runs cover earlier commits.
- Also add a `push: tags: ['v*-csci435-*']` trigger so future sprint tags get tested.

**E (median ≤15 min): not reachable with B and C as written.** That combination lands at about 17-19 min, bounded by test-unit-default plus sonar. Reaching 15 also needs:
- the compile-cache fix in finding 2 (saves about 3.5 min per test job);
- moving vitest coverage out of the `needs: test-unit` chain (sonar would then only download artifacts and scan, about 2 min);
- or sharding the unit packages.

## 3. Findings the draft missed, by severity

1. **Main has a flaky vitest test, hidden by the always-red snapcraft check.**
   - db-tests failed on push for f97f4ec96f and 51b1655aa0 (runs 43345969430, 43296442804). Both are merges of docs-only PRs (#174, #165).
   - The failure: `web_src/js/features/repo-issue-edit.test.ts` › "r quotes the selection…", "expected vi.fn() to be called 1 times, but got 2". It also failed on PR run 43088279012.
   - Compliance `frontend` doesn't run on docs-only PRs, so sonarqube is the only place this shows up. Because snapcraft keeps every main commit red, nobody noticed.
2. **The Go build cache is stale and partly useless.**
   - cache-seeder has run once ever (40807939468, Oct 29), because it triggers only on changes to `go.sum`, `.golangci.yml` or the cache files (`cache-seeder.yml:14-19`).
   - The `gobuild-…` cache (2.25 GB) is 141 commits behind main. The key is fixed per `go.sum`, so it can never be refreshed (the actions/cache key can't be overwritten).
   - The seeder warms `-race` without `-cover`, but test-unit's default pass uses `-coverprofile`, so the instrumented compile always misses the cache.
   - Fix: seed on every main push with a sha-suffixed key plus restore-keys (`go-cache/action.yml:8` forbids that for the seeder today, and that decision needs revisiting), and add `-cover` to the bindata warm step.
3. **A recurring pgsql-only failure in TestMilestoneBurndown** (3 branches, Oct 9 to Oct 27) and TestRepoCalendar (Nov 9). It looks like a real dialect or time bug, not runner noise, since both attempts of 37861291323 failed. It deserves its own issue, and it is the counterexample to C.
4. **Tags are not protected, and they trigger release-tag-version** (see claims 2 and 4). Fixing A plus adding a tag ruleset covers it.
5. **No required status checks** means a red db-tests run doesn't block a merge. If checks get added after C or B, skipped jobs report as passing. Use one aggregate `db-tests-ok` job with `if: always()` as the required check rather than listing individual jobs.
6. **Infrastructure flakes in PR history**, as opposed to test bugs:
   - proxy.golang.org stream error in `make deps-backend` (37843428225);
   - upload-artifact failure (43093562298);
   - Playwright `apt` install exit 100 producing a 2 GB log (43043959020).

   The e2e failures that are tests are browser-specific flakes ("element(s) not found" after 21 s), for example `[firefox] file-view-render.test.ts:5` (43291283979) and `[webkit] multiselect-aria.test.ts:97` (43278357008). The 20 labeler failures are `lint-pr-title` doing its job, not flakes.
7. **Low-severity noise and gaps:**
   - cron-renovate fires hourly and has been skipped 878 times, with cron-translations (108) and giteabot (109) also scheduled. Guarded, but it clutters the Actions tab.
   - test-unit, test-sqlite, test-mysql and test-e2e have no job-level `timeout-minutes`, so they default to 360 min.
   - Secrets: only `SONAR_TOKEN` exists. `GITHUB_READ_TOKEN` is harmless because the GitHub migration test (`services/migrations/github_test.go:22`) falls back to mocks.
   - Security posture is fine: all actions are pinned to a SHA, `pull_request_target` in the labeler checks out only the base SHA, and giteabot is guarded.
   - Concurrency on main pushes is keyed on `github.run_id`, so db-tests runs on main are never cancelled by rapid merges. That part of the probe came back clean.

**Title:** Main's CI is red on every push and skips most test suites, and backend PRs wait about 28 minutes for checks

```markdown
## Problem

`main`'s CI status means nothing, `main` skips most of the test suites, and backend PRs are slow for a reason we can fix.

### Main is red on every push, so real failures go unnoticed

- `release-nightly-snapcraft` has failed or been cancelled on all 99 of its runs since the fork (78 failed, 21 cancelled, 0 passed). The latest one, [run 43539275792](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43539275792), stops with `fatal: empty string is not a valid pathspec`. `snap/part-gitea-pull.sh:33` reads the newest tag with `%(tag)`, which is empty for lightweight tags, and all our `v1.27.3-csci435-*` tags are lightweight. Even with annotated tags it would fail at publish, because the repo has no Snap Store credentials and the `gitea` snap name belongs to upstream.
- `release-nightly` has never finished: 98 runs were cancelled and 1 is queued ([example](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43537000589)). Its jobs need upstream's private `namespace-profile-gitea-release-*` runners. The next push cancels each run, or GitHub drops it after 24 hours in the queue.
- `release-tag-version` matches `v1.*`, so it has run for every sprint tag, and all three runs were cancelled after sitting queued for those runners: s0 ([35251424595](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/35251424595)), s1 ([37872246874](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/37872246874)) and s2 ([40956082407](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/40956082407)). The s3 tag will do the same.
- The noise is hiding a real failure. `db-tests` failed on `main` after two docs-only merges ([43345969430](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43345969430), [43296442804](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43296442804)) with the flaky `repo-issue-edit.test.ts` test from #171. Nobody noticed, because every `main` commit was already red.

### Main never runs most of the test suites

Every integration job in `pull-db-tests.yml` has `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (lines 20, 56, 91, 188, 236), and `pull-e2e-tests.yml` runs only on pull requests too. A push to `main` runs `test-unit` and `sonarqube` (Go unit tests and Vitest coverage) and nothing else. Since PRs don't have to be up to date with `main` before merging, two PRs that each pass can break `main` together, and no integration or e2e run would show it. The Sprint 2 tag `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` (`40e0aa79`) has no test runs at all, so D8's Suite health section has no CI baseline to quote.

### Backend PRs take about 28 minutes, mostly compiling and waiting

Full backend `db-tests` runs take 23.3–30.1 min, with a median of about 27.6 (e.g. [43524265133](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43524265133)). Waiting for a runner isn't the cause: the median wait is 2 seconds. The time goes to three things:

- **A stale build cache.** `cache-seeder` has run once ([40807939468](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/40807939468), Oct 29), because it only triggers when `go.sum`, `.golangci.yml` or the cache files change. Its `gobuild-<go.sum hash>` key can never be overwritten, so the cache is now 141 commits behind `main`. It also warms the `-race` build but not `-race -cover`. As a result, each `test-unit` pass spends about 3.6 minutes compiling before the first package result, and every other Go test job compiles more than it should too.
- **Two unit-test passes in a row.** `test-unit` runs the normal pass (9.6–12.1 min) and then the `gogit` pass (9.4–11.5 min).
- **`sonarqube` waits on `test-unit`.** It has `needs: test-unit` and runs the Vitest coverage itself, so it can't start until both unit passes are done.

## Goal

`main` is green unless one of our own suites failed, it runs the integration and e2e suites after every merge and on every sprint tag, and anyone can run them against any ref. Backend PRs get the same checks as now, every database included, in noticeably less time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a push to `main` or a pushed `v1.*` tag, when CI runs, then `release-nightly`, `release-nightly-snapcraft`, `release-tag-version` and `release-tag-rc` show as skipped (not failed, cancelled or queued), and each skip condition has a same-line comment saying the workflow only runs upstream.
- [ ] AC2: Given a merge to `main`, when CI runs, then sqlite, MySQL, MSSQL and Postgres migration plus integration tests, Go unit tests, Vitest and the Playwright e2e suite all run against the merged commit. A newer merge never cancels a run that has already started.
- [ ] AC3: Given a team member opens Actions → `db-tests` or `e2e-tests` → Run workflow and enters a ref (e.g. `v1.27.3-csci435-s2`), or someone pushes a `v*-csci435-*` tag, when the run finishes, then the suites from AC2 have run against that ref.
- [ ] AC4: Given a push to `main`, when CI runs, then the Go build cache is saved again under a key tied to that commit and includes the `-race -cover` build. Given a backend PR opened after that, when `test-unit`'s normal pass runs, then the first package result appears at most 1 minute after `make test-backend` starts (about 3.6 minutes now).
- [ ] AC5: Given a backend PR, when `db-tests` runs, then the normal and `gogit` unit-test passes run as two separate jobs at the same time. Both run `make test-check`, and only the normal pass uploads Go coverage.
- [ ] AC6: Given any `db-tests` run, when it runs, then Vitest coverage runs in its own job, at the same time as the Go unit tests. `sonarqube` scans both coverage reports, and a failing Vitest test still makes the `db-tests` run fail.
- [ ] AC7: Given four backend PR runs after the fix, when they finish, then the median wall-clock time of `db-tests` is at most 20 minutes (about 27.6 now), and every job that ran on a backend PR before this change still runs. No database, `-race` or `gogit` coverage is removed.
- [ ] AC8: Given the jobs in `pull-db-tests.yml`, `pull-e2e-tests.yml` and `pull-compliance.yml`, when any of them hangs, then it stops at its own `timeout-minutes` instead of GitHub's 6-hour default.

## Out of Scope

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: stopping the upstream release workflows

**Decision:** Add `if: github.repository == 'go-gitea/gitea'` to each job in the four release workflows, the same guard upstream already uses in `cron-*.yml` and `giteabot.yml`.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Fix the release workflows to work on the fork* (annotated tags, our own runners and store accounts). The team doesn't publish binaries, images or snaps, so this would be work for nothing.
- *Delete the files, or turn them off with `gh workflow disable`.* Deleting conflicts with upstream syncs. Turning them off can't be reviewed, only shows in the settings page, and is the kind of quiet silencing the course counts as small at most.
**Rationale:** These workflows publish upstream's builds and can't run here. The guard is upstream's own pattern, it goes through review in the diff, and a code comment records why.
**Consequences:** Their runs still appear in the Actions tab, marked skipped. If the team ever publishes its own builds, the guard has to come off.

### Decision 2: cutting backend PR time

**Decision:** Refresh the build cache on every push to `main`, run the two unit-test passes as parallel jobs, and move Vitest coverage out of the `test-unit` → `sonarqube` chain. Every database job still runs on every backend PR.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Run MySQL, MSSQL and Postgres on a PR only when it touches `models/`, `modules/setting/` or `services/migrations/`.* Rejected because the Postgres-only failures in `TestMilestoneBurndown` (three branches) and `TestRepoCalendar` came from `services/issue` and `routers/`, outside those paths, so they would have reached `main` without any warning.
- *Drop `-race` or the `gogit` pass on PRs.* That would save the most time, but it removes checks without fixing anything, and the course counts that as silencing.
- *Only add more shards.* It uses more runners for the same work, so PRs would start waiting on each other because of the org's limit of 20 jobs at once.
**Rationale:** Most of the extra time is wasted compiling and jobs waiting on each other, not testing. Fixing that keeps every check and still shortens the run.
**Consequences:** One more job per backend PR. Each unit-test job sets up its own service containers. The 20-minute target is limited by the slowest database job.

### Decision 3: how the cache gets refreshed

**Decision:** `cache-seeder` runs on every push to `main`. It saves under `gobuild-<go.sum hash>-<commit sha>` with a `restore-keys` fallback to the newest entry, and warms `-race -cover` as well as `-race`. Update the comment at `.github/actions/go-cache/action.yml:7-8` to give the new reason.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Keep the key based only on `go.sum`.* A saved key can't be overwritten, so the cache never updates until `go.sum` changes.
- *Let PR jobs save the cache.* A PR's cache is only visible to that PR and the PRs based on it, so other PRs can't use it, and several jobs writing at once would fight over the same key.
**Rationale:** Caches saved from `main` are visible to every PR, and one key per commit means the newest build is always available.
**Consequences:** Each entry is about 2.25 GB against the repo's 10 GB cache limit, so GitHub keeps about four and evicts the oldest. One extra seeder run per merge.

### Decision 4: running the suites on `main` and on demand

**Decision:** Let the existing `pull-db-tests.yml` and `pull-e2e-tests.yml` jobs run on `push` to `main`, on `v*-csci435-*` tags and on `workflow_dispatch` (with a `ref` input that checkout uses), by changing each `pull_request`-only condition to `github.event_name != 'pull_request' || <the existing files-changed check>`. The concurrency group for push runs is shared and `cancel-in-progress` is false, so a running job is never cancelled.
**Alternatives Considered:**
- *A new `main-suites.yml` that copies the jobs.* The copies would drift away from the PR jobs.
- *Turn the jobs into one `workflow_call` workflow used by both.* No copies, but it rewrites upstream's files the most, which makes upstream syncs harder.
**Rationale:** Changing the conditions keeps one definition for each job and touches as few upstream lines as possible. Starting a run by hand with a `ref` input works for old tags, which don't have this workflow file.
**Consequences:** About 9 jobs per merge on `main`. When merges come in bursts, a waiting run is replaced by the newest one, so a failure may cover more than one merge. That's the trade-off in Open Questions.

## Scope

medium, `scope: medium`. Changes `pull-db-tests.yml`, `pull-e2e-tests.yml`, `pull-compliance.yml` (timeouts), `cache-seeder.yml`, the `go-cache` action and the four release workflows. No product code changes. Evidence needs several pushes to `main`, a tag push, a manual run against a tag and four timed PR runs, each checked against the before numbers.
```

```markdown
## Problem

`main`'s CI status means nothing, `main` skips most of the test suites, and backend PRs are slow for a reason we can fix.

### Main is red on every push, so real failures go unnoticed

- `release-nightly-snapcraft` has failed or been cancelled on all 99 of its runs since the fork (78 failed, 21 cancelled, 0 passed). The latest one, [run 43539275792](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43539275792), stops with `fatal: empty string is not a valid pathspec`. `snap/part-gitea-pull.sh:33` reads the newest tag with `%(tag)`, which is empty for lightweight tags, and all our `v1.27.3-csci435-*` tags are lightweight. Even with annotated tags it would fail at publish, because the repo has no Snap Store credentials and the `gitea` snap name belongs to upstream.
- `release-nightly` has never finished: 98 runs were cancelled and 1 is queued ([example](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43537000589)). Its jobs need upstream's private `namespace-profile-gitea-release-*` runners. The next push cancels each run, or GitHub drops it after 24 hours in the queue.
- `release-tag-version` matches `v1.*`, so it has run for every sprint tag, and all three runs were cancelled after sitting queued for those runners: s0 ([35251424595](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/35251424595)), s1 ([37872246874](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/37872246874)) and s2 ([40956082407](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/40956082407)). The s3 tag will do the same.
- The noise is hiding a real failure. `db-tests` failed on `main` after two docs-only merges ([43345969430](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43345969430), [43296442804](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43296442804)) with the flaky `repo-issue-edit.test.ts` test from #171. Nobody noticed, because every `main` commit was already red.

### Main never runs most of the test suites

Every integration job in `pull-db-tests.yml` has `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (lines 20, 56, 91, 188, 236), and `pull-e2e-tests.yml` runs only on pull requests too. A push to `main` runs `test-unit` and `sonarqube` (Go unit tests and Vitest coverage) and nothing else. Since PRs don't have to be up to date with `main` before merging, two PRs that each pass can break `main` together, and no integration or e2e run would show it. The Sprint 2 tag `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` (`40e0aa79`) has no test runs at all, so D8's Suite health section has no CI baseline to quote.

### Backend PRs take about 28 minutes, mostly compiling and waiting

Full backend `db-tests` runs take 23.3–30.1 min, with a median of about 27.6 (e.g. [43524265133](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43524265133)). Waiting for a runner isn't the cause: the median wait is 2 seconds. The time goes to three things:

- **A stale build cache.** `cache-seeder` has run once ([40807939468](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/40807939468), Oct 29), because it only triggers when `go.sum`, `.golangci.yml` or the cache files change. Its `gobuild-<go.sum hash>` key can never be overwritten, so the cache is now 141 commits behind `main`. It also warms the `-race` build but not `-race -cover`. As a result, each `test-unit` pass spends about 3.6 minutes compiling before the first package result, and every other Go test job compiles more than it should too.
- **Two unit-test passes in a row.** `test-unit` runs the normal pass (9.6–12.1 min) and then the `gogit` pass (9.4–11.5 min).
- **`sonarqube` waits on `test-unit`.** It has `needs: test-unit` and runs the Vitest coverage itself, so it can't start until both unit passes are done.

## Goal

`main` is green unless one of our own suites failed, it runs the integration and e2e suites after every merge and on every sprint tag, and anyone can run them against any ref. Backend PRs get the same checks as now, every database included, in noticeably less time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a push to `main` or a pushed `v1.*` tag, when CI runs, then `release-nightly`, `release-nightly-snapcraft`, `release-tag-version` and `release-tag-rc` show as skipped (not failed, cancelled or queued), and each skip condition has a same-line comment saying the workflow only runs upstream.
- [ ] AC2: Given a merge to `main`, when CI runs, then sqlite, MySQL, MSSQL and Postgres migration plus integration tests, Go unit tests, Vitest and the Playwright e2e suite all run against the merged commit. A newer merge never cancels a run that has already started.
- [ ] AC3: Given a team member opens Actions → `db-tests` or `e2e-tests` → Run workflow and enters a ref (e.g. `v1.27.3-csci435-s2`), or someone pushes a `v*-csci435-*` tag, when the run finishes, then the suites from AC2 have run against that ref.
- [ ] AC4: Given a push to `main`, when CI runs, then the Go build cache is saved again under a key tied to that commit and includes the `-race -cover` build. Given a backend PR opened after that, when `test-unit`'s normal pass runs, then the first package result appears at most 1 minute after `make test-backend` starts (about 3.6 minutes now).
- [ ] AC5: Given a backend PR, when `db-tests` runs, then the normal and `gogit` unit-test passes run as two separate jobs at the same time. Both run `make test-check`, and only the normal pass uploads Go coverage.
- [ ] AC6: Given any `db-tests` run, when it runs, then Vitest coverage runs in its own job, at the same time as the Go unit tests. `sonarqube` scans both coverage reports, and a failing Vitest test still makes the `db-tests` run fail.
- [ ] AC7: Given four backend PR runs after the fix, when they finish, then the median wall-clock time of `db-tests` is at most 20 minutes (about 27.6 now), and every job that ran on a backend PR before this change still runs. No database, `-race` or `gogit` coverage is removed.
- [ ] AC8: Given the jobs in `pull-db-tests.yml`, `pull-e2e-tests.yml` and `pull-compliance.yml`, when any of them hangs, then it stops at its own `timeout-minutes` instead of GitHub's 6-hour default.
```
